target: Quando você volta?
english: When are you coming back?
old: 'Quando você volta?' – 'Voltar' = to come back/return. Present tense used for near future plans.
focus: Simple present 'volta' = English 'are you coming back' (near-future) – make that the one rule, cut the 'voltar = return' gloss

target: Onde a gente se encontra?
english: Where do we meet up?
old: 'Onde a gente se encontra?' – reflexive 'se encontrar' = to meet up. 'A gente' = we (informal).
focus: 'A gente' (literally 'the people') = informal 'we' and takes third-person singular – one rule; drop the reflexive aside

target: Eu gosto de cozinhar para os amigos.
english: I like cooking for friends.
old: 'Gostar de' + infinitive: 'gosto de cozinhar.' 'Para os amigos' = for friends. Purpose with 'para.'
focus: 'Gostar DE' – English speakers omit the de; 'gosto de cozinhar' is the example. One rule; cut the 'para os amigos' aside

target: O que você faz da vida?
english: What do you do for a living?
old: 'O que' means 'what.' 'Fazer da vida' is the natural way to ask about someone's profession in Brazil.
focus: Keep only the 'fazer da vida' idiom – the natural way to ask about someone's profession; cut the 'O que' gloss opener.

target: Como se diz isso em português?
english: How do you say this in Portuguese?
old: 'Como' means 'how.' 'Como se diz' is the impersonal way to ask – literally 'how does one say.'
focus: Impersonal 'se' in 'como se diz' = 'how does one say' is the insight; cut the 'Como means how' gloss opener.

target: As ruas do centro estão cheias.
english: The downtown streets are crowded.
old: 'estão' (estar) – marks a temporary condition, emotion, or location. Ser would imply permanence.
focus: Anchor ser/estar in this card: 'estão cheias' = crowded right now, not by nature; de-template the stamp.

target: Nós jantamos num restaurante italiano.
english: We had dinner at an Italian restaurant.
old: Regular -ar past: jantar → jantamos. Same form as present – context ('num restaurante italiano') clarifies past.
focus: 'jantamos' is both present and past for -ar verbs – one form, two tenses; drop the conjugation-drill framing.

target: Ele gosta de acordar cedo para correr.
english: He likes waking up early to run.
old: Portuguese `gostar` always takes `de`: `gosto de pizza`, `gosto de você`. Drop the `de` and the sentence breaks. English `like` has no preposition; Portuguese needs one.
focus: Strip backticks; keep the core: gostar always needs 'de' ('gosta de acordar') where English 'like' takes no preposition.

target: Os pratos da comida mineira são fartos.
english: The dishes of Minas Gerais cuisine are generous.
old: 'são' (ser) – for permanent qualities, identity, origin. Using estar would imply a temporary state.
focus: Anchor ser in this card: 'são fartos' = inherent character of mineira cooking, hence ser not estar; de-template the stamp.

target: Meu irmão mais novo é o mais alto da família.
english: My younger brother is the tallest in the family.
old: 'Mais novo' = younger, 'mais alto' = tallest/taller. 'O mais + adjective + da' = the most...of (superlative).
focus: Lead with the superlative frame 'o mais alto da família' – Portuguese says 'of the family' where English says 'in'; cut the paired glosses.

target: Vocês gostam de churrasco?
english: Do you like barbecue?
old: Different from Spanish `gustar` (which flips the subject). Portuguese `gostar` works straightforwardly: subject + gostar + de + thing.
focus: Strip backticks; keep the one rule – gostar is subject-first + 'de' ('gostam de churrasco'), no Spanish gustar-style subject flip

target: Ainda bem que deu certo.
english: Thank goodness it worked out.
old: 'Ainda bem que' means 'thank goodness that' or 'it's a good thing that.' Expresses relief.
focus: Hook the literal logic – 'ainda bem' is literally 'still well'; one rule, cut the double re-gloss of the translation

target: A gente gosta de viajar no Carnaval.
english: We like to travel during Carnival.
old: 'A gente gosta de' – remember 'a gente' takes singular: 'gosta' not 'gostamos.' 'No Carnaval' = during Carnival.
focus: One rule only: 'a gente' means we but takes 3rd singular – 'gosta', not 'gostamos'; drop the 'no Carnaval' side-gloss

target: Ela gosta de ler antes de dormir.
english: She likes to read before bed.
old: 'Gostar de' + infinitive: 'gosta de ler.' 'Antes de' = before. 'Antes de dormir' = before sleeping.
focus: Unify into a single rule: infinitive after 'de' where English uses -ing – 'gosta de ler' (likes reading), 'antes de dormir' (before sleeping)

target: A gente pôde sair mais cedo ontem.
english: We were able to leave early yesterday.
old: 'Poder' in the past: pude, pôde, pudemos, puderam. Note the circumflex on 'pôde' (past) to distinguish from 'pode' (present).
focus: Keep only the trap: 'pôde' (past) vs 'pode' (present) – the circumflex is the only visible difference; cut the paradigm list

target: Nada a ver, não foi isso que eu disse.
english: That has nothing to do with it; that's not what I said.
old: 'Nada a ver' means 'nothing to do with it' or 'that's not it.' A very common expression for disagreement.
focus: Anchor on the literal logic: 'nada a ver' = literally 'nothing to SEE' where English says 'nothing to do with it'; cut the re-translation

target: Ele é um cara muito simpático.
english: He's a very nice guy.
old: 'Simpático' = friendly/nice. In Brazilian Portuguese, this is a very common compliment. Agrees with masculine 'cara.'
focus: Pivot to the false friend: 'simpático' = nice/friendly, NOT English 'sympathetic' (that's 'compreensivo'); drop the agreement side-note

target: Eu esqueci de comprar o pão.
english: I forgot to buy the bread.
old: Regular -er past: esquecer → esqueci (eu). 'Esquecer de' = to forget to. -er past first person: -i.
focus: Drop the conjugation mechanics; keep 'esquecer de' – Portuguese needs 'de' before the infinitive where English says 'forget to': esqueci de comprar.

target: Eu morei em Salvador por dois anos.
english: I lived in Salvador for two years.
old: Regular -ar past: morar → morei (eu). 'Por dois anos' = for two years – 'por' for duration.
focus: Drop the conjugation line; keep 'por' for duration – 'por dois anos' = for two years, where 'para' would wrongly signal purpose (the por/para trap).

target: Ele é gordo e baixo, mas muito engraçado.
english: He's fat and short, but very funny.
old: 'Gordo e baixo' – masculine adjectives matching 'ele.' Physical descriptions use 'ser' (permanent traits).
focus: One rule only: physical/permanent traits take ser – 'Ele é gordo e baixo'. Cut the adjective-agreement half (told elsewhere).

target: Nós esperávamos bom tempo, mas nevou.
english: We were expecting good weather, but it snowed.
old: Preterite narrates events (what happened); imperfect paints the scene (what was going on). They work as a pair.
focus: The insight is right and this card is the perfect anchor – quote it: 'esperávamos' paints the scene (imperfect), 'nevou' is the event (preterite).

target: Essa é a melhor pizza da cidade.
english: This is the best pizza in the city.
old: Superlatives use 'o/a mais' + adjective or irregular forms: o melhor (the best), o pior (the worst), o maior (the biggest).
focus: Anchor on the real trap in this card: after a superlative Portuguese uses de – 'a melhor pizza da cidade' = the best pizza IN the city, not 'na cidade'.

target: A escola era pequena, mas todo mundo se conhecia.
english: The school was small, but everyone knew each other.
old: 'Se' can also indicate reciprocal action: 'eles se encontram' can mean 'they meet each other'.
focus: Reciprocal se is genuinely in this card – quote it: 'todo mundo se conhecia' = everyone knew EACH OTHER; drop the off-card example.

target: O vento está forte demais para ir à praia.
english: The wind is too strong to go to the beach.
old: 'A + o/a/os/as' contracts to 'ao/à/aos/às'. The grave accent on 'à' marks the contraction a + a (crase).
focus: Anchor the crase on this card: 'ir à praia' – à is a + a squeezed together, and the grave accent is the only visible trace. Cut the full contraction table.

target: Vocês tomaram café da manhã?
english: Did you have breakfast?
old: Regular -ar past: tomar → tomaram. 'Tomar café da manhã' = to have breakfast (a set expression).
focus: Drop the conjugation line; keep the idiom: Portuguese TAKES breakfast – 'tomar café da manhã', the same tomar used for drinks.

target: Ele encontrou um emprego novo.
english: He found a new job.
old: Regular -ar past: encontrar → encontrou. 'Emprego novo' – adjective after noun is the default position.
focus: Drop the conjugation line; keep word order – adjectives follow the noun by default: 'emprego novo', not 'novo emprego'.

target: Ele parou de fumar há seis meses.
english: He stopped smoking six months ago.
old: 'Parar de' + infinitive means 'to stop doing something.' 'Há' + time means 'ago': 'há seis meses' = six months ago.
focus: One rule only: 'ha seis meses' = six months ago – ha + time span means ago; cut the parar de half

target: Ele fez questão de pagar o jantar.
english: He insisted on paying for dinner.
old: 'Fazer' past: ele fez. 'Fazer questão de' = to insist on – a common fixed expression.
focus: Lead with the idiom: 'fez questao de' = insisted on, literally made a question of; cut the fazer-past lead

target: A gente chegou atrasado por causa do trânsito.
english: We arrived late because of traffic.
old: Regular -ar past: chegar → chegou. With 'a gente,' always singular: 'a gente chegou.'
focus: 'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb: 'a gente chegou'; cut the regular-past lead

target: Eu mudei de ideia sobre a viagem.
english: I changed my mind about the trip.
old: Regular -ar past: mudar → mudei. 'Mudar de ideia' = to change one's mind (fixed expression).
focus: 'Mudar de ideia' – Portuguese changes OF something: mudar de casa, de emprego; the de is mandatory; cut the conj lead

target: A gente quis ajudar, mas ela recusou.
english: We wanted to help, but she refused.
old: 'Querer' → 'quis' (I wanted/tried). In negative preterite: 'não quis' = refused.
focus: Preterite querer = a completed act of wanting/trying: 'a gente quis ajudar'; fix the 'I wanted' person slip

target: Eu estava dormindo quando o telefone tocou.
english: I was sleeping when the phone rang.
old: Classic past contrast: imperfeito sets the scene (was sleeping = ongoing), perfeito interrupts it (rang = sudden event).
focus: Good scene-vs-interrupt insight – anchor it by quoting 'estava dormindo' and 'tocou' from this card

target: Ela perguntou se eu queria ir junto.
english: She asked if I wanted to go along.
old: Regular -ar past: perguntar → perguntou. 'Se' introduces indirect questions: 'perguntou se eu queria.'
focus: 'Perguntou se' = asked whether – se introduces indirect questions; cut the regular-past lead

target: Que pena, eu não vou poder ir.
english: What a shame, I won't be able to go.
old: 'Que pena' means 'what a shame/pity.' Very common for expressing regret or disappointment.
focus: Turn the gloss into the pattern: que + noun = 'what a...': 'Que pena' = what a shame; same shape as que legal, que sorte

target: Ela fez uma viagem incrível para Fernando de Noronha.
english: She took an incredible trip to Fernando de Noronha.
old: 'Fazer' past: ela fez. 'Fez uma viagem' = took a trip. 'Fazer viagem' is the natural expression.
focus: You MAKE a trip in Portuguese: 'fez uma viagem', never take one; cut the fazer-past lead

target: A gente curtiu muito a praia.
english: We really enjoyed the beach.
old: 'Curtir' means to enjoy/have fun. In the past: 'curti a festa' = I enjoyed the party. Very common in informal Brazilian Portuguese.
focus: 'Curtir' = informal Brazilian for enjoy/like – anchor with this card's 'curtiu a praia', not the off-card 'curti a festa'

target: Ele terminou o relatório a tempo.
english: He finished the report on time.
old: Regular -ar past: terminar → terminou. 'A tempo' = on time (just in time). 'No prazo' = by the deadline.
focus: 'A tempo' (just in time) vs 'no prazo' (by the deadline) – keep that contrast, cut the regular-past lead

target: Nós dividimos a pizza entre quatro.
english: We split the pizza among four.
old: Regular -ir past: dividir → dividimos. Same as present form – past meaning clear from 'pizza entre quatro.'
focus: Lead with the trap: 'dividimos' is both present and past – context decides; cut the regular -ir-past framing

target: A gente fez amizade com os vizinhos.
english: We became friends with the neighbors.
old: 'Fazer' past: a gente fez. 'Fazer amizade com' = to become friends with – a useful expression.
focus: You MAKE friendship in Portuguese: 'fez amizade com' = became friends with; cut the fazer-past lead

target: Vocês experimentaram o açaí daqui?
english: Did you try the açaí from here?
old: Regular -ar past: experimentar → experimentaram. 'Experimentar' = to try (food/experience). 'O açaí daqui' = the açaí from here.
focus: 'Experimentar' looks like experiment but means to try: 'experimentaram o acai'; cut the regular-past lead

target: Nós viemos de taxi porque choveu.
english: We came by taxi because it rained.
old: 'Vir' past: nós viemos. Don't confuse 'viemos' (came) with 'vimos' (saw). 'De taxi' = by taxi.
focus: 'Viemos' (we came) vs 'vimos' (we saw) – keep the confusable, cut the vir-past lead and the de taxi gloss

target: A gente combinou de se encontrar no shopping.
english: We arranged to meet at the mall.
old: Regular -ar past: combinar → combinou. 'Combinar de' = to agree to / to arrange. 'A gente combinou.'
focus: combinar de + infinitive = to arrange/agree to (literally 'combine to') – drop the conjugation lead, anchor on 'combinou de se encontrar'

target: Eu soube da notícia pelo jornal.
english: I found out the news through the newspaper.
old: 'Saber' in the past: soube, soube, soubemos, souberam. In the past, 'saber' often means 'to find out' rather than 'to know.'
focus: preterite shifts saber's meaning: soube = found out, not knew – cut the paradigm list, anchor on 'soube da noticia'

target: Vocês deram uma olhada no projeto?
english: Did you take a look at the project?
old: 'Dar' past: vocês deram. 'Dar uma olhada' = to take a look – a very common expression.
focus: dar uma olhada = literally 'give a look' = take a look, very common – drop the 'Dar past' conjugation lead

target: Nós voltamos de viagem ontem à noite.
english: We came back from the trip last night.
old: Regular -ar past: voltar → voltamos (nós). The -amos ending is the same as present! Context tells which.
focus: voltamos is BOTH past and present – lead with the ambiguity trap, note 'ontem' is what disambiguates here

target: A gente viajou para Minas Gerais no feriado.
english: We traveled to Minas Gerais on the holiday.
old: Regular -ar past: viajar → viajou. With 'a gente,' use third person singular: 'a gente viajou.'
focus: a gente means 'we' but takes 3rd-person SINGULAR: a gente viajou – lead with that trap, drop the regular-ar lead
